name: MO-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Wesley Bell running with $1.1M cash on hand
Prediction markets price Bell at 98% to win
model.rationale: The D+29 baseline, Bell's incumbency and $3.6M raised, and Polymarket pricing near 98% all point to a comfortable Democratic hold, so the forecast stays at the fundamentals-driven margin of roughly 29 points. With no polls or expert ratings, uncertainty stays moderately wide but nowhere near competitive territory.
model.watch: Any surprise polling showing Bell under 60% against Berry, or a late outside-spending surge, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Wesley Bell, a first-term Democratic incumbent, defends a St. Louis-area seat whose partisan lean is D+29, one of the most Democratic districts in Missouri. He enters the general election with strong finances: $3.6 million raised, about $1.1 million on hand, and modest outside support, while Republican Paul Berry has reported little visible fundraising or outside backing. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets put Bell's chances near 98 percent. The seat is rated Safe Democratic, with Bell favored by roughly 29 points.
